record.original_question: Let d > 1 and let f be an integrable function on R^d. Suppose f tiles R^d at some level w with a translation set Lambda subset R^d of bounded density, meaning that there exists M > 0 such that #(Lambda intersect (x + B)) <= M for every x in R^d, where B is the open unit ball in R^d. Must there exist a lattice L subset R^d such that f + L is also a tiling, possibly at a different level w'?

evidence.quote: Let f in L1(R^d), d > 1, and suppose that f tiles at some level w with a translation set Lambda subset R^d of bounded density. Does there necessarily exist a lattice L subset R^d such that f + L is also a tiling, possibly at a different level w'?
A set Lambda subset R^d is said to have bounded density if there exists M > 0 such that #(Lambda intersect (x+B)) <= M for all x in R^d, where B is the open unit ball in R^d.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d>1$ be an integer. A discrete set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is said to have bounded density if there exists $M>0$ such that $\#(\Lambda\cap(x+B))\le M$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, where $B$ denotes the open unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$. Given $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and a real number $w$, we say that $f$ tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ at level $w$ with translation set $\Lambda$ if $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda} f(x-\lambda)=w$ for almost every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$ (the series converging absolutely a.e.). For a lattice $L\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ (i.e., a discrete subgroup of $\mathbb{R}^d$ of full rank), we write $f+L$ for the tiling by the translates of $f$ along $L$.

Question: Suppose that $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ at some level $w$ with a translation set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of bounded density. Must there exist a lattice $L\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ and a real number $w'$ such that $f$ tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ at level $w'$ with translation set $L$ (i.e., $f+L$ is a tiling)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a 2020/2021 survey on translational tiling by Kolountzakis and Lev. No subsequent resolution was located in the search; partial results are known in dimension 1 and for special classes (e.g., polytopes with multiplicity), but the general higher-dimensional problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Tiling by translates of a function: results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys main results on the structure of tilings of R^d by translates of a function and lists open problems including lattice replacement under bounded density.
status_evidence.claim: The lattice-replacement question for bounded-density translation sets in R^d, d>1, is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Translational tilings by a polytope, with multiplicity
status_evidence.snippet: Studies multi-tilings by translates of a polytope and shows lattice multi-tilings exist under hypotheses, partial results in this direction.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results give lattice tilings for polytopes with multiplicity but not general L^1 functions.
